about.title: Fontana Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Fontana sits along I-10 in San Bernardino County, and a steady flow of consumer goods, vehicles, and equipment moves into homes and workplaces here every day. A tire that separates on the San Bernardino Freeway, a space heater that ignites in a home off Citrus Avenue, a power tool whose guard gives way, a child's car seat that cracks in a low-speed collision on Sierra Avenue — each of these can leave a family facing medical bills and lost work through no fault of their own. California law treats these situations differently from an ordinary negligence claim. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach past the maker to distributors and the retailer that sold it. LawProactive is a free service that connects Fontana residents with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency.

items.question: My tire failed on I-10 near Fontana and I crashed. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It may be both. Fontana recorded 799 injury collisions in 2025, and some crashes trace back to a component that failed rather than a driving error. If a tire, brake, airbag, or steering part was defective, the manufacturer or seller can be held strictly liable in California. Keep the vehicle and the part as they are so an attorney can have them examined.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was negligent?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability often runs on strict liability, so you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the maker took reasonable care is typically not the deciding issue. An attorney can evaluate which type of defect fits your case.

items.question: I still have the product that hurt me. Should I throw it away or return it?
items.answer: Hold onto it. The product itself is often the most important evidence in a defect claim, and returning or discarding it can make your case much harder to prove. Store it somewhere safe, along with the packaging, receipt, and any instructions, and photograph everything before anyone handles it. The attorney you're connected with will advise on the next steps.
